back: French policy of making colonised people culturally and legally French.
British system of governing through existing African rulers under the supervision of British officials.
French rules allowing officials to punish African subjects without trial and demand forced labour.
French governor of Senegal (1854-1861, 1863-1865) who expanded the colony and created the Tirailleurs Sénégalais.
Saint-Louis, Gorée, Rufisque and Dakar, whose African inhabitants had French citizenship rights.

front: When did Lugard's forces capture Kano and Sokoto?

back: Chiefs appointed by the British in south-eastern Nigeria, where there had been no single rulers; often resented.

front: Why did Lugard use indirect rule?
back: Few officials, little money, and the Sokoto Caliphate's existing rulers, taxes and courts could be used.
